# WSL data disk (F:) and Y: from WSL

- `/data-local` (`/home/jamesan/sam2-training`) lives in `F:\WSL\Ubuntu\ext4.vhdx`, which is all of F: (931 GB). Check
  F:'s free space (`Get-Volume -DriveLetter F`) before a sync or clone; at 0 bytes ext4 goes read-only and the disk
  later refuses to attach. The disk is sparse and mounted with `discard`, so deleting files returns space to F:.
- Docker Desktop holds the Ubuntu vhdx open even with Ubuntu stopped. For `wsl --manage Ubuntu ...` run
  `docker desktop stop`, then `wsl --shutdown`, and `docker desktop start` afterwards (every container pauses).
- Run anything non-trivial in WSL as a script in the session scratchpad:
  `wsl -d Ubuntu [-u root] -- sh /mnt/c/Users/.../scratchpad/x.sh`. Variables in `wsl -- sh -c '...'` from PowerShell
  get lost, and wsl.exe output is UTF-16: pipe through `Out-String | % { $_ -replace "`0","" }`.
- `/mnt/y` is a read-only CIFS mount (fstab). To write to Y: from WSL (approved copies only), mount the share
  read-write at a separate path (`/mnt/y_rw`, same credentials file) and use `rsync -rltH` to keep hard links
  (`cp -al` set clones); hard links work on that share. Verify by checksum with page caches dropped
  (`echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches`) before deleting a local copy.
